chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Sunday nights with Jelly Roll Morton; Sonny Clay's arrival
summary: Howard played tenor with Jelly Roll on Sunday nights until fired; Sonny Clay arrived around 1916.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Okay. Oh, and how about -- we talked a little bit about Jelly Roll the other day, but when was it you worked with him?
I worked with him down at -- it was Sunday afternoons, down at the -- oh, what's the name of that place? Okay. (Inaudible).
(Inaudible) Suzie might know that name.

Yeah, maybe we can ask here when she comes back in the room. We can ask her if she remembers the name of the club. But we didn't have the tape on. We have it on now. Tell us what you told us off the tape, that just you and Jelly Roll played together, right?
Yeah.
Hold your mike up.
Jelly Roll and myself.
And you were playing?
Saxophone.
You were playing tenor saxophone.
Tenor, yeah, uh-huh.
And just the two of you played. Was this for very long?
No, just on Sunday nights.
On Sunday nights. That must have been interesting.
Just Sunday nights for a while. Not long. I didn't play long. They kicked me out too quick. I don't think they liked my playing.
That would be hard to understand from what I've heard about your playing.
(Laughter)
They didn't like it, I don't think so.
Who didn't?
People, some people. They didn't care much about it.
Sonny Clay worked with you and he also worked with Jelly Roll, is that right?
Yeah.
Was that around that same time?
Well, Sonny Clay was just -- let's see. No, he was just playing (Inaudible). I'm trying to think of what you call it. Just the band was playing with him. That's all.
I see. It says here that Sonny Clay
moved to the West Coast around 1916. That was shortly after you came here, wasn't it? Do you remember when Sonny Clay came to L.A.?
No, I don't, but I know it was shortly after I came here, but I didn't do much playing. You know, I was too young.
Yeah. Yeah, I know, you were a teenager when you got here, right?
Yeah, I was going to school. Going to school. Had a by thug under my arm (inaudible). I can't remember too much.
